decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom serves a small, specialized niche and dropped from its own page to a mere mention in 2019, a sign of weak results against aspiration, but it fills a strategic gap in the portfolio and the firm likely has the slack to carry it.
Small volume ionization chambers are core dosimetry products that kept their own page across both observed years, so performance appears satisfactory and gives no reason to search for alternatives.
This second small volume chamber kept a dedicated page, and although it may overlap with Product B, the low cost of carrying a chamber model in an established line favors keeping it.

Standard clinical ionization chambers with several models are a staple of the established business that fits the firm's dosimetry expertise and its regulated, calibration-driven demand, so results likely meet aspirations.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the water phantom and QA workflows and kept stable web presence, so there is no visible shortfall that would trigger problemistic search.
Thimble chambers are widely used reference devices that support accredited calibration services, and their continued dedicated presence suggests satisfactory performance.
